feeds.title: Applied Social Psychology Blog
feeds.description: The purpose of the Applied Social Psychology (ASP) blog is to allow students to write about the course concepts as they observe those concepts in action in real life. Sort of like a personal news story. The trick is to start thinking like an applied social psychologist; seeing the theories and concepts in action.

feeds.title: In-Mind Blog
feeds.description: The Inquisitive Mind, or In-Mind, is In-Mind Foundation's flagship online quarterly magazine for social psychology. We publish a peer-reviewed magazine, and we'd like to think that our journal is the highest impact journal in social psychology. We aim to interact with everyone interested in everyday human concerns, informing you on the hot trends in scientific psychological research!

feeds.title: ScienceDaily » Social Psychology News
feeds.description: Provides latest news related to social Psychology.

feeds.title: PsyPost » Social Psychology
feeds.description: This section of the blog covers the latest news about social psychology and sociology research. PsyPost is a psychology and neuroscience news website dedicated to reporting research related to human behavior, cognition, and society.

feeds.title: Approaching Significance Blog
feeds.description: A methodology blog for social psychology.

feeds.title: Social Psychology Perspectives
feeds.description: We hope to build up this blog with our ideas on how research from the field of social psychology can help us make sense of events going on at our campus but also in the world around us.

feeds.title: Where Are The Grown-Ups? Blog
feeds.description: Social psychologist, Harvard Lecturer, speaker, and bestselling author Dr. Amy Cuddy is an expert on the behavioral science of power, presence, and prejudice. Amy Cuddy's Reflections On Social Science & Civility.

feeds.title: Jose L. Duarte Blog
feeds.description: Blog on social psychology, scientific validity, the misuse of statistics, and positive psychology.

feeds.title: Social PsyQ
feeds.description: Social psychology is everywhere. We help you make sense of it. We're interested in social psychology in a broad sense (the ways in which the implied or real presence of others influences people's thoughts, actions and beliefs). Specifically, we want to translate research, make social psych more accessible & begin an informal dialog about social science in the digital age. Blog by Jen and Mallory.

feeds.title: Mark Rubin's Research
feeds.description: Recent social psychology research conducted by Mark Rubin, a researcher at the University of Newcastle, Australia.

feeds.title: International Review of Social Psychology
feeds.description: The journal is aimed at all researchers, students, and professionals in social psychology. The RIPS focuses on the quality of publications in all areas of social psychology. The expertises of the texts proposed are realized by an international reading committee. The IRSP publishes literature reviews, theoretical notes and empirical research in all areas of social psychology.

feeds.title: Everyday Sociology Blog
feeds.description: A site that features interesting, informative, and, most importantly, entertaining commentary from sociologists all over the United States on topics such as pop culture, news, and everyday life.
